decisions.reason: The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY adding the SK6812 Mini-E LEDs to the complete USB-powered 3.3V rail; no additional change is required.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY recording the SK6812 Mini-E part and 3.3V supply, and the DCDC1 load-coverage change requires no further charge-status update.
Its existing normal-operation load coverage is already all system loads, so identifying the 3.3V LEDs as a DCDC1 load does not change this Requirement's state.
The candidate's current powered-load list does not include the SK6812 LEDs, so confirmation that those LEDs use 3.3V leaves the 5V boost Requirement unchanged.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY recording SK6812 Mini-E LEDs supplied at 3.3V; no additional propagated change is needed.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY that fully records the selected SK6812 Mini-E part and its 3.3V supply.
The source decision concerns LED inclusion on the powered 3.3V rail, not USB enumeration, data routing, or standalone-programming capability.
Adding 3.3V LEDs to DCDC1 load coverage does not change battery cutoff thresholds or electrical-protection behavior.
The LED supply decision does not change the battery NTC connector, monitoring function, or thermal-protection controller.
The source decision does not resolve or alter the battery connector family, pin count, pin functions, part number, or ambiguous pin order.
The DCDC1 load-coverage change has no necessary effect on the established four-layer power-board stack.
Confirming the LED voltage and DCDC1 supply role does not change the number or identity of the project's separate boards.
